aliases: ternary alternative with xor (owner prompt, 12 Oct 2026)
plain_what: Store each weight as -1, 0 or +1, so using it needs only add, subtract or skip, and compare two bit patterns by counting how many bits differ. The aim is cheap multiplier-free arithmetic. The dense ternary sum was assessed and not adopted; the bit-counting and three-valued switches now live inside the discrete model.
how_it_works: Ternary weights w in {-1,0,+1} are stored in two bit planes: P is set where w=+1, N where w=-1, and P AND N = 0 (the repo's lowbit code uses 2 bits per weight, CODE_POS=1, CODE_NEG=2, so the planes are the two bits). For a binary activation vector X the dot product is exact: sum w_i x_i = popcount(P AND X) - popcount(N AND X). The zero case is free (skip). Multi-bit activations repeat this per bit-plane and combine with shifts and adds; a power-of-two row scale is a shift. XOR is not the ternary dot product: XOR gives Hamming distance d(a,b) = popcount(a XOR b), a distance whose signed-sum use needs |a| + |b| - 2|a AND b|. Against GF(2), -1 and +1 collapse into one element, so 'ternary XOR matmul' is false as stated. What is true: the multiplier disappears but the sum over all W x D weights stays dense, so the matmul does not. In the discrete model the same ingredients appear as routing parts: a coordinate Hamming count breaks equal L1 displacement ties when a transported query chooses a port, and ternary trit gates (candidates visited in the order 0, -1, +1) switch flock levels on or off. No bitsliced contraction or GPU popcount kernel exists in the tree.
geometry: Not a lattice mechanism by itself: Boolean hypercube / GF(2) bit planes. Inside the discrete model it acts on 8D integer root coordinates of the E8 anchor orbit and on ternary (base-3) FBS binders; E8 is the (8,4,4) Hamming code lifted to a lattice (Construction A, verified in the 26 Sep note), but Hamming distance on E8 labels is not the E8 lattice metric (D32).

status_reason: As proposed (a dense ternary/XOR contraction replacing matmul) it was assessed and not adopted: it removes the multiplier, not the dense sum (D25; docs/mechanisms/ternary-xor-arithmetic.md). It was never trained in, and the post-hoc ternary head export lost (7.416 vs 7.171 bits). Its Hamming and trit-gate parts run inside discrete-learning and flock-read.
reopen_conditions: A GPU kernel for the bitsliced or lookup-table ternary contraction exists and is exact against TernaryLinear::forward_i32 for both binary and 8-bit activations, with host fallback refused (D24).

A pre-registered rung trains it in from step 0, not as a post-hoc snap of a float master, against the matched icosian-mantissa arm at equal steps, width and weight bytes, with at least 2 seeds or 200 fresh rows; bar = larger of 0.01 BPB or 2x measured noise, set before compute.
Tokens/s on the same CUDA harness goes up, not only MACs or bytes touched; the D11 engine lost 68.0 vs 127.5 tok/s, and product-key memory lost the same way, so this is the bar to beat.

The contraction is applied where it is not a dense W x D sum (a routed or selected subset), or the owner rules it an accepted, labelled non-geometric arithmetic substitution (open question 5 of the brief), before any run.
Or the alphabet is made geometric: three values that are actual group elements (for example Eisenstein cube roots, a sub-ring of Z[phi]) rather than a truncated scalar quantiser.

rule_compat.D11: Compatible in form: add/subtract/skip and AND+popcount need no multiplier, and a power-of-two scale is a shift. Not shown to be fast: the one multiplier-free engine measured (D11 on a 29M stack) ran 68.0 tok/s against 127.5 on the float path, bit-exact (d11-serving-2026-10-10).
rule_compat.D23: No softmax or squashing in the mechanism; scoring is a hard count. Nothing to scan.
rule_compat.D30: A ternary weight contraction is still a dense W x D sum, which D25 says a handwritten dense contraction cannot replace; it would not pass as a matmul substitute. The Hamming tie-break and trit gates inside routing are not matmul.
rule_compat.D32_D37: D32 names ternary and Hamming computation as the preferred substrate and the active discrete model uses ternary gates and coordinate Hamming. D37 allows float training, but the dense-matmul ban stays, so a ternary master would need new offline sheet with an export gap.

failed_only_on_configuration: Dense ternary recurrence saturated an int32 state: a failure of an unnormalised, ungated, dense recurrence, not of ternary weights in a normalised or routed structure (the takeover review withdrew the broader reading).
Post-hoc ternary head export lost to the empirical head: a quantiser applied to a float master with a reduced search; it says nothing about weights trained ternary from the start.
Ternary readout refit missed its 0.30-bit bar: one frozen-state refit; the 0.13-bit gain is real and the integer kernel reproduced it exactly.
The D11 engine ran slower than the float path: one engine on one laptop where weight bytes, not multipliers, are scarce; it measures operation substitution on a dense contraction.
Hamming sign bits cost 0.014 bits/byte as final LM scores: shows they should admit candidates, not rank them; the retained use already follows that.
open_questions: Which operand is binary? Weight-side ternary alone gives conditional adds, not XOR; the XOR arm needs planar activations, and today's activations are integer Q formats.
Is {-1,0,+1} compatible with the project's exact Z[phi] objects, or only a coarser version of the icosian Cayley-table read?
At what depth D does the inter-plane shift-and-add reduction stop beating a conditional-add loop on the actual GPU?
If ternary wins on cost and ties on quality, is it a KEEP for a labelled non-geometric substitution or a demotion of the exact-coefficient family? This is an owner decision.
Does the discrete model's ternary gate (Parameter::Gate) help language quality at all, once a corpus run isolates it?
